investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck unscheduled, causing the eval runner to time out before any VM identity or state can be observed. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source-code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have claimed all available slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability.

[Possible] A quota or limit range on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at the namespace or cluster level is set too low relative to concurrent demand from the eval runner and any live workloads.
[Possible] One or both kata-capable nodes may be cordoned, tainted, or in a NotReady state, reducing effective capacity below what the resource count alone would suggest.

[Less likely] The node affinity/selector expression in the remote agent pod spec may have become overly restrictive (e.g., a label changed on the eligible nodes), shrinking the schedulable node set to fewer than the 2 that previously worked.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 eligible nodes immediately to determine current used vs. allocatable counts. If fully consumed, identify and terminate any leaked or idle remote agent pods that are holding slots.

Review whether the eval runner's withCleanup() mechanism (run-status-probes.mjs) is reliably releasing remote agent VMs after each probe run. If cleanup is failing, prior eval runs may be leaking VM resource reservations.

Assess whether the cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (currently 2 nodes worth of slots) is sufficient for the expected concurrent load from both live workloads and observability eval runs. If not, plan node pool expansion or quota adjustment.

Verify that both kata-capable nodes are in Ready state and are not cordoned or carrying blocking taints that would prevent the remote agent pod from being scheduled even when resource slots are available.

Once scheduling is restored, re-run all three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm the feature returns to a passing state and all required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are collected.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the eval runner that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before attempting remote agent creation, so the failure message can distinguish capacity exhaustion from other scheduling errors more explicitly.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration or a scheduler bug.

If the remote agent pod spec's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector was found to exclude the 2 kata-capable nodes (e.g., due to a label change), the root cause would be a selector misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run with no other concurrent workloads succeeded and produced all 4 required evidence keys, the failure would be attributable to transient resource contention rather than a persistent capacity shortfall.
If the 2 kata-capable nodes were found to be cordoned or NotReady at the time of the failure, the root cause would be node availability rather than resource exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared scheduling dependency would be ruled out and the failure would be localized to the create path specifically.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts on all nodes and fails with a warning when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.

Add an eval that enumerates all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and alerts if any have been running beyond a maximum expected lifetime, catching leaked VM reservations before they exhaust the pool.

Add a node-readiness eval that checks the Ready status and schedulability (no blocking taints, not cordoned) of all nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm label, so node-level unavailability is surfaced independently of the remote agent creation check.

Refine the remote-agent-create eval to distinguish between Unschedulable due to resource exhaustion vs. node affinity mismatch by parsing the scheduler message, enabling more targeted alerting and faster triage.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-26T16:30–16:35Z with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could not be scheduled, the remote agent VM was never provisioned, and the runner never reached the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out as Unschedulable, preventing the eval runner from creating an agent, polling its state, or collecting any required evidence. This is a resource-capacity and/or node-affinity configuration failure in the production Kubernetes cluster, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.

Preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable quantity reduced, capacity would drop to zero.

TERTIARY — Cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes: if the node pool that carries the kata peer-pods extended resource does not autoscale, a burst of concurrent remote-agent requests (including eval probes) can exhaust capacity with no automatic recovery.

UNLIKELY — Eval runner misconfiguration causing it to request more kata.peerpods.io/vm resources than intended per pod: would require a change to the pod spec, and no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck unscheduled, causing the eval runner to time out before any VM identity or state can be observed. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source-code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 124s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 143s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 141s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState were never written because createAgent() (run-status-probes.mjs:1885) never produced a schedulable pod.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before any VM was assigned.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=131021 — the probe ran for ~131s before failing, matching the scheduler's unschedulable window reported in the message.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the resulting pod is never scheduled, no VM id or state is ever returned to the evidence collector.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have claimed all available slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability.

[Possible] A quota or limit range on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at the namespace or cluster level is set too low relative to concurrent demand from the eval runner and any live workloads.
[Possible] One or both kata-capable nodes may be cordoned, tainted, or in a NotReady state, reducing effective capacity below what the resource count alone would suggest.

[Less likely] The node affinity/selector expression in the remote agent pod spec may have become overly restrictive (e.g., a label changed on the eligible nodes), shrinking the schedulable node set to fewer than the 2 that previously worked.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration or a scheduler bug.

If the remote agent pod spec's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector was found to exclude the 2 kata-capable nodes (e.g., due to a label change), the root cause would be a selector misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run with no other concurrent workloads succeeded and produced all 4 required evidence keys, the failure would be attributable to transient resource contention rather than a persistent capacity shortfall.
If the 2 kata-capable nodes were found to be cordoned or NotReady at the time of the failure, the root cause would be node availability rather than resource exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared scheduling dependency would be ruled out and the failure would be localized to the create path specifically.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts on all nodes and fails with a warning when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.

Add an eval that enumerates all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and alerts if any have been running beyond a maximum expected lifetime, catching leaked VM reservations before they exhaust the pool.

Add a node-readiness eval that checks the Ready status and schedulability (no blocking taints, not cordoned) of all nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm label, so node-level unavailability is surfaced independently of the remote agent creation check.

Refine the remote-agent-create eval to distinguish between Unschedulable due to resource exhaustion vs. node affinity mismatch by parsing the scheduler message, enabling more targeted alerting and faster triage.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-26T16:30–16:35Z with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could not be scheduled, the remote agent VM was never provisioned, and the runner never reached the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out as Unschedulable, preventing the eval runner from creating an agent, polling its state, or collecting any required evidence. This is a resource-capacity and/or node-affinity configuration failure in the production Kubernetes cluster, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable quantity reduced, capacity would drop to zero.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-26T16:33–16:35Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 nodes and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. The other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity/selector constraints at all. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request is stuck Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream remote-agents eval checks to fail before any evidence can be collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity with free slots, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a pod spec misconfiguration or scheduler bug.
If a remote-agent pod successfully schedules and reaches Running state during the same window, the failure would be intermittent rather than a full capacity exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod was recently changed to exclude previously-matching nodes, the root cause would be a configuration regression rather than capacity exhaustion — source evidence for such a change is not present in this packet.

If the local-agent-runtime or other non-remote checks also began failing with scheduling errors in the same window, the problem would be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool and would implicate a cluster-wide scheduling issue.
If the eval runner logs show the pod was scheduled but the agent API returned an error, the scheduling exhaustion diagnosis would be incorrect and the failure would be in the agent runtime layer.
